clue.text: In the afternoon, everybody meets everybody in the game

indicators.note: the clue puts everybody in the afternoon, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: PM, post meridiem, marks the afternoon
everybody means all
everybody again means all

explanation.surface: A sociable afternoon where every guest gets to meet every other guest while playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts ALL inside PM, making PALLM; a second ALL follows. Pall-mall was an old mallet-and-ball game that gave London's Pall Mall its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall-mall is a historic lawn game played by striking a wooden ball through an iron hoop with a mallet.

clue.text: Shakespearean ensign's weapon

definitions.meaning: the swaggering ensign who serves Falstaff in Henry IV and Henry V is named ...

explanation.surface: An officer in a Shakespeare play and the arm he carries.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The ensign character in Shakespeare's history plays bears this name, and a handgun is the same word.

clue.text: German breaks fast time (over an hour) for the distance

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over, above, what follows
the German letter breaks into the fasting season, splitting it open

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
h is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A German interrupts a long fast, running past an hour, to cover some ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' puts G inside LENT to give LENGT; 'over' sets that above H in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is the measure of how far something extends, the distance from end to end.

clue.text: Rodent hurt cat when climbing

parts.note: to mar is to damage or hurt

indicators.note: in a down clue a climbing word is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A small animal is injured by a cat as it scrambles up after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns TOM upwards in the down entry, giving MOT after MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmot is a burrowing ground squirrel of mountain regions, a member of the rodent order.

clue.text: A small case about a member's place to put a bulb

indicators.note: the small case goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: a locket is a small case worn on a chain, holding a picture
MP is a Member of Parliament; with the 's it gives MPS

explanation.surface: A tiny container wrapped round a politician's belongings, somewhere to fit a light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A + MPS inside LOCKET: L-AMPS-OCKET. The second 'a' supplies the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp socket is the fitting into which a light bulb is screwed or pushed.

clue.text: Save speculation for flier

parts.note: save in the sense of except, which bar also means
a bet is a speculative wager

explanation.surface: An investor's advice: keep your money rather than gamble it on something flighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb, but it means 'except', like 'bar' in 'all bar one'. A flier here is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The barbet is a stout-billed tropical bird, and anything that flies can be called a flier.

clue.text: Sanction for Poplar organisation to tour V&A

indicators.note: the rearranged letters travel round, enclosing, the museum's initials
organisation signals the letters being arranged into a new order

parts.note: the Victoria and Albert Museum in London is known as the V&A

explanation.surface: Permission sought for a group from Poplar, an East London district, to visit a famous museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges POPLAR into APPROL; 'to tour' puts VA inside it: APPRO-VA-L.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval and sanction are synonyms, both meaning official permission or endorsement.

clue.text: Capital asset supports family

parts.note: supports means bears, as in bears a weight; in a down clue it also sits above, supporting, the family
kin are family members

explanation.surface: A financial phrase: an investment that underpins a household.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue BEARS stands above KIN. A bearskin is the tall fur hat worn by guards outside Buckingham Palace, a sight of the capital, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The guardsman's tall fur hat is a familiar feature of London ceremony, so the clue calls it an asset of the capital.

clue.text: The player is the one in a tizzy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the single article is placed in the state of agitation

parts.note: to be in a tizzy is to be in a spin, so a tizzy is a spin
A is used as 'one', the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Picking out the flustered one in the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside SPIN to give SPIAN, after THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, someone who plays parts on stage.

clue.text: Roy mends damaged set of indicators

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters are broken up and put back differently

explanation.surface: A man called Roy repairs a broken set of warning lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the letters of ROY MENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a group of symptoms that together indicate a condition.

clue.text: Drug one consumed after minor operation

indicators.note: the one who ate comes after the operation in the answer

parts.note: op is a short form of operation
I is the Roman numeral one
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A patient eats after a small procedure and is given medication.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic drug derived from opium, such as morphine.

clue.text: Shed you once found in river

indicators.note: the old pronoun is found within the river's name, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river
thou is an old word for you

explanation.surface: Someone from long ago is discovered in a river after a hut is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts THOU inside OUSE: OU-THOU-SE. The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is an outbuilding, such as a shed, standing apart from the main house.

clue.text: Half-hearted deities taste scandal

indicators.note: the word for deities loses half of its two middle letters, half its heart

parts.note: gods are deities
to sip is to taste a little

explanation.surface: Unenthusiastic gods sample some salacious rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' removes D, one of the two heart letters OD of GODS, leaving GOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk about others' private affairs, much like scandal.

clue.text: British offices show consent for witchcraft?

parts.note: offices are rooms for work
to tick a box is to show consent

explanation.surface: British workplaces approve something to do with magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witchcraft?' reads as magic, but means a craft, a vehicle, flown by a witch; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch traditionally flies on one, making it a witch's craft, or flying vehicle.

clue.text: Disfigurement faces Roman with a disease

indicators.note: the mark faces, stands in front of, what follows in an across answer

parts.note: a scar is a disfigurement
Latin was the language of the Romans

explanation.surface: A scarred face confronts a Roman who has an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' puts SCAR in front of LATIN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatina is another name for scarlet fever, an infectious illness.

clue.text: A turn in the troika is done

indicators.note: the turn goes in the Russian vehicle

parts.note: a troika is a Russian sleigh drawn by three horses, a kind of sled
to wind is to turn, as a key or a road does

explanation.surface: A Russian sleigh ride with a turn that ends the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts WIND inside SLED. 'done' is slang for cheated, as in 'I've been done'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be done is slang for being cheated or conned, so done means cheated.

clue.text: Inhibit student in unfamiliar surroundings

indicators.note: the student is placed in the unfamiliar setting

parts.note: unfamiliar surroundings are strange ones
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student feels held back in a new environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside STRANGE. L, from a learner's plate, stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle a project is to stifle or inhibit it.

clue.text: Furiously cram stuffing into furniture

indicators.note: doing something furiously throws the letters into disorder

parts.note: horsehair was the traditional stuffing for upholstery

explanation.surface: Frantically packing filling into a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furiously' rearranges CRAM into ARMC, then HAIR follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a padded seat with arms, an item of furniture.

clue.text: Later, women cooked fruit

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed and transformed

explanation.surface: Some women prepare a fruit dish later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges LATER and WOMEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: The watermelon is a large juicy fruit of the gourd family.

clue.text: Leading man in 10

parts.note: the hero is the leading man in a story

explanation.surface: A star actor appears in a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 refers to the answer to 10 across, a drug: this answer is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroin is a narcotic made from morphine, an example of an opium-derived drug.

clue.text: To do a favour one has globe manufactured

indicators.note: the rearranged globe has, holds, the numeral inside it
manufactured signals the letters are made into something new

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone helps out by making a globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges GLOBE into OBLGE; 'has' puts I inside: OBL-I-GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to help them by doing them a kindness.

clue.text: Sweat round jowl

parts.note: drops of sweat are like dew
a lap is a round of a track

explanation.surface: Perspiration around someone's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewlap is a fold of loose skin hanging from the neck, like a jowl.

clue.text: Subtlety of sister touring a church

indicators.note: the sister tours round, enclosing, the article

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun goes round a church with refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts A inside NUN: NU-A-N, then CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a fine shade of meaning, a subtle difference.

clue.text: Marshal's astute about place to eat, on reflection

indicators.note: the clever word goes about, around, the eating place

parts.note: astute means able, capable

indicators.note: reflection reverses the letters, as a mirror does

parts.note: a mess is where soldiers eat

explanation.surface: A military officer is clever about where to dine, after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns MESS into SSEM; 'about' puts it inside ABLE: A-SSEM-BLE. 'Marshal' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops is to gather and arrange them, to assemble them.

clue.text: Record and preserve an impasse

parts.note: a log is a written record
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: Writing down and keeping things leads to deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage or deadlock, a situation where progress halts.

clue.text: Man with boil I treated having a two-part name

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a man with a boil, a patient with a double-barrelled name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges MAN, BOIL and I together.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a binomial is a species name of two parts, genus and species.

clue.text: It's tiresome showing appreciation in sterile environment

indicators.note: the barren word forms an environment around the appreciation

parts.note: dry means barren or sterile
an ear for music is an appreciation of it

explanation.surface: Applauding in a sterile setting is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' puts EAR inside DRY: DR-EAR-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and wearisome, just as tiresome does.

clue.text: Superficial trickle contains mould

indicators.note: the trickle holds the type inside it

parts.note: to seep is to trickle
a mould is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A small leak harbours fungal growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts KIND inside SEEP. 'mould' suggests fungus but means a type, as in 'cast in the same mould'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep goes no further than the surface, so it is superficial.
